BURHAN:v2p277/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p277/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BURHAN:v2p277/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda treats إذ in “Do they hear you when you call?” as an extra particle.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative, like the preceding anecdote, serves the same preaching purpose and also ends with the recurring verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.anchor: the purpose of narrating this anecdote is the same as the one intended for the previous one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.claim: The Abraham account fills the gap after Noah in the previous sūrah because Abraham was the most prominent messenger between Noah and Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.anchor: the most prominent messenger between Noah (sws) and Moses (sws) was Abraham (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.claim: Abraham’s questions expose the idols’ baselessness; the people have no answer and persist only because they follow their forefathers, a tradition they will not abandon.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.anchor: because they are only following the ways of their forefathers, which they will not give up at any cost

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.claim: The reported events occur after Abraham had conclusively conveyed the truth through both scriptural and intellectual arguments.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.anchor: when he had conclusively communicated the truth to his people through both scriptural and intellectual arguments

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p161/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p161/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p161/r10.claim: Abraham then exposes their lack of sense by asking about attributes absent from the idols and found only in God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p161/r10.anchor: ولما أجابوا إبراهيم، أخذ يوقفهم على قلة عقولهم، باستفهامه عن أوصاف مسلوبة عنهم لا يكون ثبوتها إلا لله تعالى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r1.claim: The majority read يسمعونكم from سمع; its object structure depends on whether the thing heard is explicitly audible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يسمعونكم، من سمع وسمع إن دخلت على مسموع تعدت إلى واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r2.speaker: الفارسي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r2.claim: Al-Fārisī says سمع takes two objects when followed by something not itself audible, with an audible action as the second object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r2.anchor: فمذهب الفارسي أنها تتعدى إلى اثنين، وشرط الثاني منهما أن يكون مما يسمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r3.claim: He prefers the analysis that سمع takes one object, with the following action functioning circumstantially; here the non-audible object is explained by an omitted noun such as دعاءكم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r3.anchor: والصحيح أنها تتعدى إلى واحد، وذلك الفعل في موضع الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes يسمعونكم to mean that the idols answer you.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r5.speaker: قتادة ويحيى بن يعمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r5.claim: They read the verb in the form أسمع, with its second object omitted and understood as the answer or speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r5.anchor: وقرأ قتادة، ويحيى بن يعمر: بضم الياء وكسر الميم من أسمع، والمفعول الثاني محذوف تقديره: الجواب، أو الكلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r6.claim: إذ may be treated loosely as إذا, or the present تدعون may be understood as occupying a past-tense position; adding إذ to a present clause is a cue for this shift.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r6.anchor: وإذ: ظرف لما مضى، فإما أن يتجاوز فيه فيكون بمعنى إذا، وإما أن يتجاوز في المضارع فيكون قد وقع موقع الماضي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the present tense a portrayal of the past scene as it unfolded, making the rebuke more forceful than asking whether the idols ever heard them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وجاء مضارعا مع إيقاعه في إذ على حكاية الحال الماضية التي كنتم تدعونها فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r8.claim: The reading may pronounce the ذ of إذ clearly or assimilate it into the ت of تدعون.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r8.anchor: وقرىء: بإظهار ذال إذ وبإدغامها في تاء تدعون.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says a قياس-based form with the ذ assimilated into the following ت is possible, though no one read it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويجوز فيه قياس مذكر، ولم يقرأ به أحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r10.claim: He rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s analogy: replacing ت with د is restricted to particular افتعل forms and a few exceptions, not the imperfect prefix ت.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r10.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكر أنه يجوز فيه قياس مذكر لا يجوز، لأن ذلك الإبدال، وهو إبدال التاء دالا، لا يكون إلا في افتعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r11.claim: If this kind of assimilation occurs, the ذ changes to ت and merges with ت, yielding اتخرج, rather than changing the prefix ت into د.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163/r11.anchor: بل إذا أدغم مثل هذا أبدل من الذال تاء وأدغم في التاء، فتقول: اتخرج.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r1.claim: The question asks whether idols hear their prayer, or whether they hear them praying, with the omitted wording inferred from context.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r1.anchor: أيسمعون دعاءكم أو يسمعونكم تدعون فحذف ذلك لدلالة

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r2.claim: Another reading means do they hear your answer to the prayer; the present tense with إذ vividly reenacts the past scene.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r2.anchor: أي يسمعونكم الجواب عن دعائكم ومجيئه مضارعا مع { إذ } على حكاية الحال الماضية استحضارا لها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r1.claim: The interrogative exposes that lacking even one divine attribute precludes divinity; lacking all of them makes the idols' claim still more untenable.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r1.anchor: مع كل عاقل إذا تعقل أن لا تصح رتبة الإلهية مع فقد واحدة منها , فكيف مع فقدها كلها ؟

BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r2.claim: The shift from a past time adverb to a present verb evokes the whole span of worship and rebukes them by asking whether the idols ever heard them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r2.anchor: معبرا بظرف ماض وفعل مضارع تنبيها على استحضار جميع الزمان

AKHFASH:v2p461/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p461/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p461/r3.claim: هل يسمعونكم can mean whether they hear anything from you or hear your supplication, with الدعاء omitted; a Basit poet's line about حكمات الأبق illustrates the ellipsis, and الأبق means flax.
AKHFASH:v2p461/r3.anchor:
قال الشاعر: [من البسيط وهو الشاهد الحادي والستون بعد المئتين] :
القائد الخيل منكوبا دوابرها * قد أحكمت حكمات القد والأبقا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r6.claim: Since a lord is sought in need and expected to benefit or harm, Abraham asks whether the idols hear their calls or can help or hurt, exposing their lack of divinity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r6.anchor: ولما كان شأن الرب أن يلجأ إليه في الحاجة وأن ينفع أو يضر ألقى إبراهيم عليهم استفهاما عن حال هذه الأصنام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r7.claim: Idolaters worship images in hope of benefit or to ward off harm; some also worshipped devils.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r7.anchor: وكانت الأمم الوثنية تعبد الوثن لرجاء نفعه أو لدفع ضره ولذلك عبد بعضهم الشياطين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r9.claim: Abraham opens the debate in order to leave the idolaters unable to prove that their images hear, benefit, or harm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p139/r9.anchor: وأراد إبراهيم فتح المجادلة ليعجزوا عن إثبات أنها تسمع وتنفع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r8.claim: Most readers have yasmaʿūnakum with fatḥa on yāʾ; Qatāda reads it with ḍamma from asmaʿa, with the object omitted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بفتح الياء من «يسمعونكم» ، وقرأ قتادة بضمها من أسمع وبكسر الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r9.claim: Some readers pronounce the dhāl and tāʾ separately in idh tadʿūn; most assimilate them after changing dhāl to tāʾ, while the predicted doubled-dāl form is not used because of the following root dāl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p233#4/r9.anchor: وقرأ جماعة من القراء إذ تدعون بإظهار الذال والتاء، وقرأ الجمهور إذ تدعون بإدغام الذال في التاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.claim: The people concede that their idols do not hear, benefit, or harm; they follow their ancestors' practice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.anchor: اعترفوا بأن (1) أصنامهم لا تفعل شيئا من ذلك، وإنما رأوا آباءهم كذلك يفعلون

JISHUMI:v7p5362/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5362/r5.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v7p5362/r5.claim: The common reading has yasmaʿūnakum with fatḥa on yāʾ and mīm.

JISHUMI:v7p5362/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5362/r6.speaker: بعضهم
JISHUMI:v7p5362/r6.claim: Some read yasmaʿūnakum with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on mīm.
JISHUMI:v7p5362/r6.anchor: وعن بعضهم بضم الياء وكسر الميم

NAHHAS:v3p182/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p182/r3.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v3p182/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies an omitted object: ‘Do they hear from you?’ or ‘Do they hear your supplication?’ He cites an anonymous poetic line about reins of flax whose omitted noun is understood from context; al-abq means flax.
NAHHAS:v3p182/r3.anchor: قال الأخفش فيه حذف والمعنى هل يسمعون منكم أو هل يسمعون دعائكم

NAHHAS:v3p182/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p182/r4.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v3p182/r4.claim: Qatāda is reported to read with a ḍamma on yāʾ, yielding ‘Do they make you hear their voices when you call?’
NAHHAS:v3p182/r4.anchor: وروي عن قتادة أنه قرأ ( قال هي يسمعونكم ) بضم الياء

NAHHAS:v3p182/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p182/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p182/r5.claim: The dhāl of idh may be assimilated into the following tāʾ.
NAHHAS:v3p182/r5.anchor: وإن شئت أدغمت الذال في التاء

MUQATIL:26:69-85/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r4.claim: Abraham asks whether the idols answer their prayers, benefit them when worshipped, or harm them if neglected.
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r4.anchor: يقول: هل تجيبكم الأصنام إذا دعوتموهم،

QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r9.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r9.claim: He says هل يسمعونكم contains an ellipsis: it means ‘do they hear from you?’ or ‘do they hear your prayers?’; a line of poetry similarly omits a complement, and الأبق is glossed as flax (or hemp in al-Sihah).

QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r10.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r10.claim: He reports a reading with damma on the ya, asking whether the idols make their worshippers hear their sounds.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r10.anchor: وروي عن قتادة أنه قرأ { هل يسمعونكم } بضم الياء أي هل يسمعونكم أصواتهم

RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r7.claim: Al-Kashshāf says ‘Do they hear you?’ requires an omitted noun: ‘Do they hear your supplication when you call?’
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r7.anchor: لا بد في يسمعونكم من تقدير حذف المضاف معناه هل يسمعون دعاءكم

RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r8.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r8.claim: Qatādah reads the question as asking whether the idols hear and answer their supplication.
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r8.anchor: وقرأ قتادة { هل يسمعونكم } أي هل يسمعونكم الجواب عن دعائكم

RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r9.claim: The reasoning is that worshippers seek help from those they worship, expecting them to hear their requests and grant benefit or avert harm; idols cannot fulfill this role.
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r9.anchor: يلتجىء إليه في المسألة ليعرف مراده إذا سمع دعاءه ثم يستجيب له في بذل منفعة أو دفع مضرة

TABATABAI:26:70-75/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:70-75/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:70-75/r4.claim: Abraham’s first objection is that worship expresses the worshiper’s need and humility and entails invocation; invocation requires the object to hear and know the request, which inert idols cannot do.
TABATABAI:26:70-75/r4.anchor: العبادة تمثيل لذلة العابد وحاجته إلى المعبود فلا يخلو من دعاء من العابد للمعبود

TABRISI:26:72-77/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:72-77/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:72-77/r1.claim: Aqdam means what existed before another, like awwal and asbaq; qadar is existence with no beginning; tabrīz means displaying or making something manifest; ghāwī is one who acts in a way that forfeits reward; kabkabū is emphatic reduplication of kabb and means to tumble groups into Hell; ḥamīm is a beloved close friend whose affection is mutual.
TABRISI:26:72-77/r1.anchor: الأقدم الموجود قبل غيره ومثله الأول والأسبق والقدر وجود الشيء لا إلى أول والتبريز الإظهار

TABRISI:26:72-77/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:72-77/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:72-77/r2.claim: The verb “hear you” ordinarily takes a sound as its object; when a person is its object, it takes two objects with the second denoting audible speech or reading, never an inaudible action.
TABRISI:26:72-77/r2.anchor: هل يسمعونكم أصله أن يتعدى إلى ما كان صوتا مسموعا تقول سمعت كلامك فإن وقع على جوهر تعدى إلى مفعولين

TABRISI:26:72-77/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:72-77/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:72-77/r3.claim: “Do they hear you when you call?” deletes the noun “your call,” as the clause “when you call” makes clear.
TABRISI:26:72-77/r3.anchor: على حذف المضاف والتقدير هل يسمعون دعاءكم فحذف المضاف ودل عليه قوله إذ تدعون

TABRISI:26:72-77/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:72-77/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:72-77/r13.claim: Abraham asks whether the idols hear their supplications, answer them, benefit them, or harm them if left; religion must rest on proof, or he would not have argued this way.
TABRISI:26:72-77/r13.anchor: معناه هل يستجيبون دعاءكم إذا دعوتموهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r5.claim: Qatāda explains Abraham's question as asking whether their gods answer them when they call on them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r5.anchor: قال قتادة: أي: هل تجيبكم آلهتكم إذا دعوتموهم.

SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r1.claim: An ellipsis is required: either they hear your invocation, making the verb take one object, or they hear you invoking, making it take two; al-Fārisī treats the supplied clause as the second object, while others make it circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r1.anchor: لا بد من محذوف أي: يسمعون دعاءكم، أو يسمعونكم تدعون

SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r2.speaker: قتادة ويحيى بن يعمر
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r2.claim: Qatāda and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read yusmiʿūnakum with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on mīm; the second object is omitted, meaning they make you hear the answer.
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r2.anchor: وقرأ قتادة ويحيى بن يعمر بضم الياء وكسر الميم

SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r3.claim: Idh is governed by the preceding verb; both verbs are past in meaning despite future forms, since the first governs idh and idh governs the second.
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r3.anchor: { إذ تدعون } منصوب بما قبله، فما قبله وما بعده

SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r4.claim: Some grammarians take idh here to mean idhā, when.
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: " إذ " هنا بمعنى إذا

SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads it as a vivid recollection of past circumstances, telling the idolaters to recall their invocations and answer whether the idols heard them; this sharpens the rebuke.
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " إنه على حكاية الحال الماضية

SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r6.claim: A prior discussion noted readings that assimilate the dhāl of idh into tāʾ or pronounce it distinctly.
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r6.anchor: وإظهارها في التاء. وقال ابن عطية

SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests applying the assimilation analogy of words like mudakkir here; it would yield a doubled dāl followed by a vowelless dāl.
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويجوز فيه قياس " مدكر " ونحوه

SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r8.claim: Al-Shaykh rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya's analogy: assimilation applies to the infix tāʾ in specified derived forms or a pronoun suffix, not the imperfect prefix tāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:26:72/r8.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا لا يجوز؛ لأن هذا الإبدال

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r2.claim: قال begins a fresh clause prompted by a question raised by the detailed description of the idolaters' reply.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r2.anchor: استئناف مبني على سؤال نشأ من تفصيل جوابهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r3.speaker: الفارسي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r3.claim: Al-Farisi says when سماع takes an object that is not itself heard, it governs two objects: كم is the first, while a second, تدعون, is omitted and supplied by the following clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r3.anchor: ومذهب الفارسي أنه حينئذ يتعدى إلى إثنين ولابد أن يكون الثاني مما يدل على صوت

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r4.speaker: غيره
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r4.claim: Other grammarians say سماع then governs one object; a following explicit or understood phrase is a circumstantial clause with a definite object or an adjective with an indefinite one, and apposition is also possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r4.anchor: ومذهب غيره أنه حينئذ متعد إلى واحد وإذا وقعت بعده ملفوظة أو مقدرة فهي في موضع الحال منه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r5.claim: Alternatively, the verb may take a genuinely heard object, with دعاءكم understood after deleting its governing noun because إذ تدعون signals it.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r5.anchor: هل يسمعون دعاءكم فحذف المضاف لدلالة ( إذ تدعون ) أيضا عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r6.claim: A proposed figurative sense is 'answer': the idols would answer the worshippers, as in the supplication 'a prayer that is not heard' and 40:60's 'You hear supplication.'
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r6.anchor: وقيل : السماع هنا بمعنى الاجابة كما في قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم انى أعوذ بك من دعاء لايسمع

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r7.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the apparent sense of hearing because it better suits the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r7.anchor: والأولى ابقاؤه على ظاهر معناه فانه أنسب بالمقام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r8.speaker: قتادة ويحيى بن يعمر
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r8.claim: Qatada and Yahya ibn Ya'mar read يسمعونكم with the form أسمع; this may favor the answer interpretation, with an omitted second object meaning 'the answer.'
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r8.anchor: نعم ربما يقال : ان ما قيل أوفق بقراءة قتادة ويحيى بن يعمر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r9.claim: إذ is a past-time adverb, while the present verb vividly recalls and stages the past scene; هل's usual future force is no problem because the hearing follows the invocation.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r9.anchor: وجيء بالمضارع لاستحضار الحال الماضية وحكايتها واما كون هل تخلص المضارع للاستقبال فلا يضر هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r10.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r10.claim: Abu Hayyan says one must construe إذ as إذا or the present verb as past; Al-Alusi prefers vivid recollection as more forceful in exposing the idolaters' failure.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r10.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : لابد من التجوز في ( إذ ) بأن تجعل بمعنى إذا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r11.claim: A reading assimilates the ذ of إذ into the ت of تدعون by changing ذ to ت and merging the consonants.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94/r11.anchor: وقريء بادغام ذال ( إذ ) في تاء ( تدعون ) وذلك بقلبها تاء وادغامها في التاء

DURR-FULL:v6p305/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p305/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p305/r4.claim: Qatāda explains Abraham’s question as asking whether their gods answer when they call them.
DURR-FULL:v6p305/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {فنظل لها عاكفين} قال: عابدين {قال هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون} يقول: هل تجيبكم

DURR-FULL:v6p305/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p305/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p305/r5.claim: ʿIkrima reads the question literally: can the idols hear your voices?
DURR-FULL:v6p305/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه في قوله {هل يسمعونكم} قال: هل يسمعون أصواتكم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r1.claim: Qatāda explains the question as asking whether the deities answer their worshippers when called.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r1.anchor: وبه عن قتادة قال : هل يسمعونكم اذ تدعون ؟ هل تجيبكم الهتكم اذا دعوتموهم ؟

BURSEVI:v6p204/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p204/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p204/r1.claim: The opening question is a resumption explaining the preceding exchange.

BURSEVI:v6p204/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p204/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p204/r2.claim: The question means whether idols hear their invocations; a genitive is omitted because the addressee itself is not audible.
BURSEVI:v6p204/r2.anchor: أي : يسمعون دعاءكم على حذف المضاف فإن كم ليس من قبيل المسموعات

BURSEVI:v6p204/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p204/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p204/r3.claim: The plural masculine form reflects the idolaters' treating their idols as rational beings.
BURSEVI:v6p204/r3.anchor: والواو بحسب زعمهم فإنهم كانوا يجرون الأصنام مجرى العقلاء

BURSEVI:v6p204/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p204/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p204/r4.claim: The phrase means the time when they call on the idols with their needs and expect a response.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r1.claim: The question means: do they hear your supplication?
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى هل يسمعونكم والمعنى هل يسمعون دعاءكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وابن يعمر وعاصم الجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r2.claim: These readers pronounce the verb with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on mīm.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r2.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير وابن يعمر وعاصم الجحدري هل يسمعونكم بضم الياء وكسر الميم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the ذ may be pronounced distinctly or assimilated into ت; assimilation is better Arabic because the sounds are close.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج إن شئت بينت الذال وإن شئت أدغمتها في التاء وهو أجود في العربية لقرب الذال

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r3.claim: ʿUkūf is adherence to something, as in iʿtikāf.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r4.claim: Benefit is good; its opposite, ḍarr, is harm that befalls.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r4.anchor: والنفع: الخير الحسن، ونقيضه الضر وهو الضرر يلحقه.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r5.claim: Aqdam, asbaq, and awwal are synonyms; qidam is existence without a beginning or in the eternal past.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r5.anchor: والأقدم والأسبق والأول نظائر، والقدم وجود الشيء لا إلى أول، وقيل: الموجود فيما لم يزل،

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī says qidam applies literally only to God and metaphorically to others.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r6.anchor: ولا يوصف به إلا القديم سبحانه حقيقة، ويستعمل في غيره مجازا عند أبي علي،

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r7.speaker: أبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r7.claim: Abū Hāshim holds that qidam applies literally to both.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r7.anchor: ويستعمل في غيره مجازا عند أبي علي، وعند أبي هاشم حقيقة فيهما.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r8.claim: Khizy is disgrace exposing sin; the source lists its verbal forms.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r8.anchor: والخزي: الفضيحة بالتعبير على الذنب، خزي يخزى خزيا، وأخزاه الله إخزاء، وهذا موقف خزي.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r9.claim: Tabrīz is emergence from concealment; its root is appearing.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r9.anchor: والتبريز: تمكن الظهور بالخروج من الخبية، وأصله الظهور، برز يبرز بروزا.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r10.claim: A ghāwī acts in ways bringing disappointment in good; related forms are listed.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r10.anchor: والغاوي: العامل بما يوجب الخيبة من الخير، غوي يغوي غيا وغواية، وأغواه إغواء.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r11.claim: Naṣr is assistance in repelling affliction.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r12.claim: Kabb is casting face down; kabkaba is tumbling into a hollow, and the doubled form is compared to ṣarṣar.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r12.anchor: والكب: الإلقاء على الوجه، كببته لوجهه كبا، والكبكبة: تدهور الشيء في هوة حتى يستقر

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r13.claim: Ikhtiṣām is mutual dispute; related forms are listed.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r13.anchor: والاختصام: منازعة كل واحد صاحبه، اختصما اختصاما، وتخاصما تخاصما، وخاصمه مخاصمة.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r14.claim: Taswiya is giving one thing what is given to another.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r14.anchor: والتسوية: إعطاء أحد الشيئين مثل ما يعطى الآخر، يقال: سوى بينهما تسوية.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r15.claim: A shāfiʿ seeks benefit or protection from harm for another; the root means addition.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r15.anchor: والشافع: السائل لغيره في جلب نفع ودفع ضرر، وأصله الضم، يقال: هو من الشفع خلاف الوتر.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r16.claim: A ṣadīq is a companion whose affection is sincere and free of admixture, from truth.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r16.anchor: والصديق: الصاحب الذي يصدق المودة، وصدق المودة: إخلاصها من الشوائب، أخذ من الصدق.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r18.claim: The phrase ellipses “your supplication”; the omitted genitive complement is replaced by its dependent, as in 12:82.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r18.anchor: قلنا: في الكلام حذف، أي: يسمعون دعاءكم، فحذف المضاف وأقام المضاف إليه مقامه كقوله: (واسأل القرية).

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r19.claim: Rational pronouns for idols reflect worshippers' belief that they benefit and harm like rational beings.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r19.anchor: قلنا: لأنهم اعتقدوا فيها النفع والضرر كمن يعقل، فكنى عنها بكنايتهم.

JISHUMI:v7p5363/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r20.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r20.claim: Alternatively, rational worshipped beings are included with nonrational ones, so the rational class governs agreement.
JISHUMI:v7p5363/r20.anchor: وقيل: لأن في المعبود من يعقل ومن لا يعقل فغلب من يعقل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p322#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p322#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p322#3/r1.claim: Abraham knew they worshipped idols; he asked to show these objects did not deserve worship, like asking a trader about his property before pointing out that slaves are not property.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p322#3/r1.anchor: كان إبراهيم عليه السلام يعلم أنهم عبدة أصنام ؛ ولكنه سألهم ليريهم أن ما يعبدونه ليس من استحقاق العبادة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r1.claim: The construction omits a possessive noun: the question is whether the idols hear your invocation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r1.anchor: لا بد في { يسمعونكم } من تقدير حذف المضاف ، معناه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r2.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r2.claim: Qatāda reads it as asking whether the idols hear the response to the invocation and can answer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r2.anchor: وقرأ قتادة : ( يسمعونكم ) ، أي : هل يسمعونكم الجواب عن دعائكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r3.claim: The present-tense verb appears with past-time إذ to portray the past situation as ongoing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r3.anchor: وجاء مضارعا مع إيقاعه في إذ على حكاية الحال الماضية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r4.claim: Recreating the past makes the hearers recall each invocation and ask whether the idols ever heard or answered, sharpening the rebuke.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p323/r4.anchor: استحضروا الأحوال الماضية التي كنتم تدعونها فيها ، وقولوا هل سمعوا أو أسمعوا قط .

NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#5/r1.claim: Ibrahim's question omits the genitive complement your invocation, understood from when you call.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#5/r1.anchor: هل يسمعون دعاءكم على حذف المضاف

STUDYQURAN:26:71/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:71/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:71/r1.claim: The exchange recalls 20:91, where Israelites tell Aaron they will remain devoted to their idol, and 20:97, where Moses confronts them about that devotion.
STUDYQURAN:26:71/r1.anchor: Similar language is used in 20:91, where the Israelites tell Aaron regarding their new idol

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r1.speaker: أبو علي، النحويون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī and other grammarians supply an omitted مضاف: do the idols hear your calls? Hearing someone as object means hearing what the person says.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r1.anchor: قال أبو علي وغيره من النحويين: هل يسمعون دعاءكم، فحذف المضاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r2.claim: The syntax is compared with Fāṭir 35:14, where those invoked do not hear the invocation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r2.anchor: ونحو ذلك من المفعولات التي تسمع، وهذا كقوله: {إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم} [فاطر: 14]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās asks whether the idols answer or hear their invocation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هل يجيبونكم أو يسمعون دعاءكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r4.claim: Muqātil glosses hearing as answering; whoever hears responds, as in the prayer phrase سمع الله لمن حمده.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p63#4/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: هل يجيبونكم إذ تدعوهم (¬4). وتفسير السمع بالإجابة معنى؛ لأن من سمع أجاب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r5.claim: The Qur'anic هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون أو ينفعونكم أو يضرون illustrates هل followed by coordinated alternatives in a single inquiry.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r5.anchor: فجرى هذا مجرى قوله عز وجل

BURHAN:v3p147/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p147/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p147/r5.claim: In the question whether the idols hear you when you call them, the implied object is your invocation, as the verse saying they do not hear your call confirms.
BURHAN:v3p147/r5.anchor: ﴿ هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون ﴾ 6 أي هل يسمعون دعاءكم بدليل الآية الآخرى

BURHAN:v2p331/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p331/r3.speaker: الكندي
BURHAN:v2p331/r3.claim: Al-Kindī says many scholars let هل share the hamza's force of report and rebuke in هل يسمعونكم.
BURHAN:v2p331/r3.anchor: قال الكندي ( 2 ) ذهب كثير من العلماء في قوله تعالى ﴿ هل يسمعونكم ﴾

BURHAN:v2p331/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p331/r4.speaker: أبو علي
BURHAN:v2p331/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects that analysis of هل يسمعونكم, which al-Kindī considers understandable because the expression is a form of denial.
BURHAN:v2p331/r4.anchor: الا اني رايت أبا علي أبي ذلك وهو معذور فان ذلك من قبيل الانكار

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r3.claim: The object is omitted from harm both to suit the cadence and to leave harm general: idols cannot harm worshippers or their enemies, unlike the specified benefit they seek for themselves.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r3.anchor: والآخر: أن الإنسان يخشى من يستطعي أن يلحق به الضرر
